diff --git a/compat/win32/exit-process.h b/compat/win32/exit-process.h
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000000..d53989884cfb0c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/compat/win32/exit-process.h
@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+#ifndef EXIT_PROCESS_H
+#define EXIT_PROCESS_H
+
+/*
+ * This file contains functions to terminate a Win32 process, as gently as
+ * possible.
+ *
+ * At first, we will attempt to inject a thread that calls ExitProcess(). If
+ * that fails, we will fall back to terminating the entire process tree.
+ *
+ * For simplicity, these functions are marked as file-local.
+ */
+
+#include <tlhelp32.h>
+
+/*
+ * Terminates the process corresponding to the process ID and all of its
+ * directly and indirectly spawned subprocesses.
+ *
+ * This way of terminating the processes is not gentle: the processes get
+ * no chance of cleaning up after themselves (closing file handles, removing
+ * .lock files, terminating spawned processes (if any), etc).
+ */
+static int terminate_process_tree(HANDLE main_process, int exit_status)
+{
+	HANDLE snapshot = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0);
+	PROCESSENTRY32 entry;
+	DWORD pids[16384];
+	int max_len = sizeof(pids) / sizeof(*pids), i, len, ret = 0;
+	pid_t pid = GetProcessId(main_process);
+
+	pids[0] = (DWORD)pid;
+	len = 1;
+
+	/*
+	 * Even if Process32First()/Process32Next() seem to traverse the
+	 * processes in topological order (i.e. parent processes before
+	 * child processes), there is nothing in the Win32 API documentation
+	 * suggesting that this is guaranteed.
+	 *
+	 * Therefore, run through them at least twice and stop when no more
+	 * process IDs were added to the list.
+	 */
+	for (;;) {
+		int orig_len = len;
+
+		memset(&entry, 0, sizeof(entry));
+		entry.dwSize = sizeof(entry);
+
+		if (!Process32First(snapshot, &entry))
+			break;
+
+		do {
+			for (i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
+				if (pids[i] == entry.th32ProcessID)
+					break;
+				if (pids[i] == entry.th32ParentProcessID)
+					pids[len++] = entry.th32ProcessID;
+			}
+		} while (len < max_len && Process32Next(snapshot, &entry));
+
+		if (orig_len == len || len >= max_len)
+			break;
+	}
+
+	for (i = len - 1; i > 0; i--) {
+		HANDLE process = OpenProcess(PROCESS_TERMINATE, FALSE, pids[i]);
+
+		if (process) {
+			if (!TerminateProcess(process, exit_status))
+				ret = -1;
+			CloseHandle(process);
+		}
+	}
+	if (!TerminateProcess(main_process, exit_status))
+		ret = -1;
+	CloseHandle(main_process);
+
+	return ret;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Determine whether a process runs in the same architecture as the current
+ * one. That test is required before we assume that GetProcAddress() returns
+ * a valid address *for the target process*.
+ */
+static inline int process_architecture_matches_current(HANDLE process)
+{
+	static BOOL current_is_wow = -1;
+	BOOL is_wow;
+
+	if (current_is_wow == -1 &&
+	    !IsWow64Process (GetCurrentProcess(), &current_is_wow))
+		current_is_wow = -2;
+	if (current_is_wow == -2)
+		return 0; /* could not determine current process' WoW-ness */
+	if (!IsWow64Process (process, &is_wow))
+		return 0; /* cannot determine */
+	return is_wow == current_is_wow;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Inject a thread into the given process that runs ExitProcess().
+ *
+ * Note: as kernel32.dll is loaded before any process, the other process and
+ * this process will have ExitProcess() at the same address.
+ *
+ * This function expects the process handle to have the access rights for
+ * CreateRemoteThread(): PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION,
+ * PROCESS_VM_OPERATION, PROCESS_VM_WRITE, and PROCESS_VM_READ.
+ *
+ * The idea comes from the Dr Dobb's article "A Safer Alternative to
+ * TerminateProcess()" by Andrew Tucker (July 1, 1999),
+ * http://www.drdobbs.com/a-safer-alternative-to-terminateprocess/184416547
+ *
+ * If this method fails, we fall back to running terminate_process_tree().
+ */
+static int exit_process(HANDLE process, int exit_code)
+{
+	DWORD code;
+
+	if (GetExitCodeProcess(process, &code) && code == STILL_ACTIVE) {
+		static int initialized;
+		static LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE exit_process_address;
+		PVOID arg = (PVOID)(intptr_t)exit_code;
+		DWORD thread_id;
+		HANDLE thread = NULL;
+
+		if (!initialized) {
+			HINSTANCE kernel32 = GetModuleHandleA("kernel32");
+			if (!kernel32)
+				die("BUG: cannot find kernel32");
+			exit_process_address =
+				(LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)(void (*)(void))
+				GetProcAddress(kernel32, "ExitProcess");
+			initialized = 1;
+		}
+		if (!exit_process_address ||
+		    !process_architecture_matches_current(process))
+			return terminate_process_tree(process, exit_code);
+
+		thread = CreateRemoteThread(process, NULL, 0,
+					    exit_process_address,
+					    arg, 0, &thread_id);
+		if (thread) {
+			CloseHandle(thread);
+			/*
+			 * If the process survives for 10 seconds (a completely
+			 * arbitrary value picked from thin air), fall back to
+			 * killing the process tree via TerminateProcess().
+			 */
+			if (WaitForSingleObject(process, 10000) ==
+			    WAIT_OBJECT_0) {
+				CloseHandle(process);
+				return 0;
+			}
+		}
+
+		return terminate_process_tree(process, exit_code);
+	}
+
+	return 0;
+}
+
+#endif

From e412431e1bf5673a529c80bb61697104ba81c0b8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2017 00:23:26 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 287/290] mingw: add a Makefile target to copy test artifacts

The Makefile target `install-mingit-test-artifacts` simply copies stuff
and things directly into a MinGit directory, including an init.bat
script to set everything up so that the tests can be run in a cmd
window.

Sadly, Git's test suite still relies on a Perl interpreter even if
compiled with NO_PERL=YesPlease. We punt for now, installing a small
script into /usr/bin/perl that hands off to an existing Perl of a Git
for Windows SDK.

Signed-off-by: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
---
 config.mak.uname | 56 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 56 insertions(+)

diff --git a/config.mak.uname b/config.mak.uname
index 784d1691c1c54c..307ec88e2dfdee 100644
--- a/config.mak.uname
+++ b/config.mak.uname
@@ -740,6 +740,62 @@ else
 		NO_PYTHON = YesPlease
 	endif
 endif
+ifeq (i686,$(uname_M))
+	MINGW_PREFIX := mingw32
+endif
+ifeq (x86_64,$(uname_M))
+	MINGW_PREFIX := mingw64
+endif
+
+	DESTDIR_WINDOWS = $(shell cygpath -aw '$(DESTDIR_SQ)')
+	DESTDIR_MIXED = $(shell cygpath -am '$(DESTDIR_SQ)')
+install-mingit-test-artifacts:
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/usr/bin'
+	printf '%s\n%s\n' >'$(DESTDIR_SQ)/usr/bin/perl' \
+		"#!/mingw64/bin/busybox sh" \
+		"exec \"$(shell cygpath -am /usr/bin/perl.exe)\" \"\$$@\""
+
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)'
+	printf '%s%s\n%s\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' >'$(DESTDIR_SQ)/init.bat' \
+		"PATH=$(DESTDIR_WINDOWS)\\$(MINGW_PREFIX)\\bin;" \
+		"C:\\WINDOWS;C:\\WINDOWS\\system32" \
+		"@set GIT_TEST_INSTALLED=$(DESTDIR_MIXED)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/bin" \
+		"@`echo "$(DESTDIR_WINDOWS)" | sed 's/:.*/:/'`" \
+		"@cd `echo "$(DESTDIR_WINDOWS)" | sed 's/^.://'`\\test-git\\t" \
+		"@echo Now, run 'helper\\test-run-command testsuite'"
+
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git'
+	sed 's/^\(NO_PERL\|NO_PYTHON\)=.*/\1=YesPlease/' \
+		<GIT-BUILD-OPTIONS >'$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/GIT-BUILD-OPTIONS'
+
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/t/helper'
+	install -m755 $(TEST_PROGRAMS) '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/t/helper'
+	(cd t && $(TAR) cf - t[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9] lib-diff) | \
+	(cd '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/t' && $(TAR) xf -)
+	install -m755 t/t556x_common t/*.sh '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/t'
+
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/templates'
+	(cd templates && $(TAR) cf - blt) | \
+	(cd '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/templates' && $(TAR) xf -)
+
+	# po/build/locale for t0200
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/po/build/locale'
+	(cd po/build/locale && $(TAR) cf - .) | \
+	(cd '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/test-git/po/build/locale' && $(TAR) xf -)
+
+	# git-daemon.exe for t5802, git-http-backend.exe for t5560
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/bin'
+	install -m755 git-daemon.exe git-http-backend.exe \
+		'$(DESTDIR_SQ)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/bin'
+
+	# git-upload-archive (dashed) for t5000
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/bin'
+	install -m755 git-upload-archive.exe '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/bin'
+
+	# git-difftool--helper for t7800
+	install -m755 -d '$(DESTDIR_SQ)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/libexec/git-core'
+	install -m755 git-difftool--helper \
+		'$(DESTDIR_SQ)/$(MINGW_PREFIX)/libexec/git-core'
 endif
 ifeq ($(uname_S),QNX)
 	COMPAT_CFLAGS += -DSA_RESTART=0

From 31a7626d7b6f706f65a770839dad15c2cfee75bf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2018 00:24:29 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 288/290] mingw: really handle SIGINT

Previously, we did not install any handler for Ctrl+C, but now we really
want to because the MSYS2 runtime learned the trick to call the
ConsoleCtrlHandler when Ctrl+C was pressed.

With this, hitting Ctrl+C while `git log` is running will only terminate
the Git process, but not the pager. This finally matches the behavior on
Linux and on macOS.

Signed-off-by: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
---
 compat/mingw.c | 9 +++++++++
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+)

diff --git a/compat/mingw.c b/compat/mingw.c
index cbc04782a71b20..6aa6930bddc15f 100644
--- a/compat/mingw.c
+++ b/compat/mingw.c
@@ -3790,7 +3790,14 @@ static void adjust_symlink_flags(void)
 		symlink_file_flags |= 2;
 		symlink_directory_flags |= 2;
 	}
+}
 
+static BOOL WINAPI handle_ctrl_c(DWORD ctrl_type)
+{
+	if (ctrl_type != CTRL_C_EVENT)
+		return FALSE; /* we did not handle this */
+	mingw_raise(SIGINT);
+	return TRUE; /* we did handle this */
 }
 
 #ifdef _MSC_VER
@@ -3826,6 +3833,8 @@ int wmain(int argc, const wchar_t **wargv)
 #endif
 #endif
 
+	SetConsoleCtrlHandler(handle_ctrl_c, TRUE);
+
 	maybe_redirect_std_handles();
 	adjust_symlink_flags();
 	fsync_object_files = 1;

From 49dc0b9428d5388eab9ea8b0b2fb3baf95e2ecec Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Neeraj K. Singh" <neerajsi@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2021 14:22:42 -0700
Subject: [PATCH 289/290] mingw: do not call xutftowcs_path in mingw_mktemp

The `xutftowcs_path` function canonicalizes absolute paths using GetFullPathNameW.
This canonicalization may change the length of the string (e.g. getting rid of \.\),
which breaks callers that pass the template string in a strbuf and expect the
length of the string to remain the same.

In my particular case, the tmp-objdir code is passing a strbuf to mkdtemp and is
breaking since the strbuf.len is no longer synchronized with strlen(strbuf.buf).

Signed-off-by: Neeraj K. Singh <neerajsi@microsoft.com>
Signed-off-by: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
---
 compat/mingw.c | 5 ++++-
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/compat/mingw.c b/compat/mingw.c
index 591c96caa268cc..dd02a5d6f839f7 100644
--- a/compat/mingw.c
+++ b/compat/mingw.c
@@ -1253,8 +1253,11 @@ char *mingw_mktemp(char *template)
 	int offset = 0;
 
 	/* we need to return the path, thus no long paths here! */
-	if (xutftowcs_path(wtemplate, template) < 0)
+	if (xutftowcsn(wtemplate, template, MAX_PATH, -1) < 0) {
+		if (errno == ERANGE)
+			errno = ENAMETOOLONG;
 		return NULL;
+	}
 
 	if (is_dir_sep(template[0]) && !is_dir_sep(template[1]) &&
 	    iswalpha(wtemplate[0]) && wtemplate[1] == L':') {

From 048b5980f37b9620ffe8580ad215c2ecc17cea3c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2021 11:26:41 +0100
Subject: [PATCH 290/290] Partially un-revert "editor: save and reset terminal
 after calling EDITOR"

In e3f7e01b50be (Revert "editor: save and reset terminal after calling
EDITOR", 2021-11-22), we reverted the commit wholesale where the
terminal state would be saved and restored before/after calling an
editor.

The reverted commit was intended to fix a problem with Windows Terminal
where simply calling `vi` would cause problems afterwards.

To fix the problem addressed by the revert, but _still_ keep the problem
with Windows Terminal fixed, let's revert the revert, with a twist: we
restrict the save/restore _specifically_ to the case where `vi` (or
`vim`) is called, and do not do the same for any other editor.

This should still catch the majority of the cases, and will bridge the
time until the original patch is re-done in a way that addresses all
concerns.

Signed-off-by: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
---
 editor.c | 8 ++++++++
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+)

diff --git a/editor.c b/editor.c
index 008c04fe2f6e0a..ba31e84ece5461 100644
--- a/editor.c
+++ b/editor.c
@@ -4,6 +4,7 @@
 #include "strvec.h"
 #include "run-command.h"
 #include "sigchain.h"
+#include "compat/terminal.h"
 
 #ifndef DEFAULT_EDITOR
 #define DEFAULT_EDITOR "vi"
@@ -55,6 +56,7 @@ static int launch_specified_editor(const char *editor, const char *path,
 		return error("Terminal is dumb, but EDITOR unset");
 
 	if (strcmp(editor, ":")) {
+		int save_and_restore_term = !strcmp(editor, "vi") || !strcmp(editor, "vim");
 		struct strbuf realpath = STRBUF_INIT;
 		struct child_process p = CHILD_PROCESS_INIT;
 		int ret, sig;
@@ -83,7 +85,11 @@ static int launch_specified_editor(const char *editor, const char *path,
 			strvec_pushv(&p.env, (const char **)env);
 		p.use_shell = 1;
 		p.trace2_child_class = "editor";
+		if (save_and_restore_term)
+			save_and_restore_term = !save_term(1);
 		if (start_command(&p) < 0) {
+			if (save_and_restore_term)
+				restore_term();
 			strbuf_release(&realpath);
 			return error("unable to start editor '%s'", editor);
 		}
@@ -91,6 +97,8 @@ static int launch_specified_editor(const char *editor, const char *path,
 		sigchain_push(SIGINT, SIG_IGN);
 		sigchain_push(SIGQUIT, SIG_IGN);
 		ret = finish_command(&p);
+		if (save_and_restore_term)
+			restore_term();
 		strbuf_release(&realpath);
 		sig = ret - 128;
 		sigchain_pop(SIGINT);

patch_expl.rag:
The patch identified by commit ID `91b07972d93aaa9e67d6fd2ce3c2d776c2872532` was submitted as a pull request at `https://github.com/prati0100/git-gui/pull/85`. This patch is associated with a workaround that advises avoiding the use of Git GUI for cloning, especially from untrusted sources, to mitigate potential security risks. The advisory suggests that if avoiding Git GUI is not feasible, users should at least refrain from cloning from untrusted sources. The patch is part of a security advisory discussion available at `https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/security/advisories/GHSA-v4px-mx59-w99c`.

The patch identified by commit ID `98d736c01e9642cd5d5c5716dba6cffd65890316` addresses an issue in the `winansi` component where `NtQueryObject` under Wine could return success without filling out a name, leading to a potential crash due to a NULL pointer dereference. The patch adds code to check the `Buffer` and `Length` to ensure robustness against this behavior, which is based on the behavior of `NtQueryObject` under Wine and ReactOS.

The patch identified by commit ID `f6e0b9f38987ad5e47bab551f8760b70689a5905` addresses an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the `pretty` component. This issue could be triggered when parsing an incomplete padding format string passed via `--pretty=format` or in Git archives when files are marked with the `export-subst` gitattribute.

The patch identified by commit ID `d96ea538e8dd0fcf381089a3b09c0a9af3617351` is associated with the release of Git version 2.32.5. The patch includes updates to the documentation and versioning files to reflect this release, as indicated by the creation of `Documentation/RelNotes/2.32.5.txt`.

The patch identified by commit ID `2f345a0b1e3934a2e59af94d52b6e9115afdb195` documents Git for Windows' security policies in the `SECURITY.md` file. This patch involves changes to the documentation to describe policies related to security issues and supported versions, as recommended by GitHub.

exploit_steps.rag:
The vulnerability described can be exploited by following these steps:

1. **Environment or Setup Needed:**
   - The target environment must have Git GUI installed, which is a graphical tool that comes with Git for Windows.
   - The environment should be such that the user is using Git GUI to clone repositories.

2. **Input Format or Payload Used:**
   - A malicious repository must be prepared with an `aspell.exe` file placed in its top-level directory. This executable is intended to be run by Git GUI during its post-processing phase after cloning.

3. **Functions or Files Involved in Triggering the Vulnerability:**
   - The vulnerability is triggered by the Git GUI's clone functionality. Specifically, the Tcl/Tk script implementation of Git GUI automatically executes `aspell.exe` if it is found in the current directory after cloning.

4. **Expected Behavior that Confirms Successful Exploitation:**
   - Successful exploitation is confirmed when the `aspell.exe` from the malicious repository is executed by Git GUI without user inspection, leading to the execution of untrusted code.

This process exploits the design flaw in Tcl on Windows, where the search path for executables includes the current directory, allowing the execution of potentially malicious code.

root_cause.rag: An integer overflow vulnerability exists in the function `pretty.c::format_and_pad_commit()` where a `size_t` is improperly stored as an `int`, and then added as an offset to a subsequent `memcpy()` call. This overflow can be triggered directly by a user running a command that processes the padding operators (e.g., %<(, %<|(, %>(, %>>(, or %><( )). The vulnerability affects the `git log` functionality when displaying commits using an arbitrary format with its --format specifiers, and is also exposed to `git archive` via the export-subst gitattribute. This can result in arbitrary heap reads and writes, potentially leading to remote code execution.

secure_coding_violation.rag:
1. The code snippet indicates a heap-buffer-overflow issue in `pretty.c:1712` during the execution of `format_and_pad_commit`. This suggests a violation of secure coding practices related to memory management, specifically accessing memory beyond the allocated buffer, which can lead to memory corruption and potential security vulnerabilities.

2. The code also demonstrates an out-of-bounds read issue, as indicated by the AddressSanitizer error in `attr.c:375`. This is a violation of secure coding practices as it involves reading memory outside the bounds of an allocated buffer, which can lead to information leakage or undefined behavior.

3. The Git GUI vulnerability highlights a violation of secure coding practices by executing untrusted code without user inspection. patch_expl.rag: The patch is identified by the Git commit ID 49a8ec9dac3cec6602f05fed1b3f80a549c8c05c and addresses a vulnerability in Git for Windows, specifically in the `gitk` component. The issue involved `gitk` potentially running executables from the current directory on Windows, which could be exploited through social engineering to execute untrusted code. The patch ensures safe path lookup by modifying the way `exec` and `open` commands handle command-line arguments, preventing inadvertent execution of executables in the worktree. exploit_steps.rag:
The vulnerability described involves the execution of untrusted code when `gitk` is run on Windows. The following steps outline the actions required to exploit this vulnerability:

1. **Environment Setup:**
   - The target environment must be a Windows system with Git for Windows installed, specifically a version prior to 2.39.2.
   - The user must have access to a repository or directory where they can place malicious executables.

2. **Input Format or Payload:**
   - Place a malicious executable in the current directory where `gitk` will be executed. This executable should be named in a way that it is inadvertently called by `gitk`.

3. **Functions or Files Involved:**
   - The vulnerability is triggered when `gitk` is executed. The `exec` function in Tcl, which is used by `gitk`, searches for executables in the current directory before searching the `PATH`.

4. **Expected Behavior:**
   - When `gitk` is run, it inadvertently executes the malicious executable placed in the current directory.
   - Successful exploitation is confirmed if the malicious code is executed, which could be verified by observing the effects of the payload or any output it generates.

The vulnerability relies on social engineering to trick users into running `gitk` in a directory containing the malicious executable.

remote_exploitability.rag: The access vector is "LOCAL," indicating that the attacker needs direct access to the system. The context does not provide any indication that the vulnerability can be triggered remotely.

root_cause.rag: A vulnerability exists in Git for Windows prior to version 2.39.2, where the `gitk` tool on Windows inadvertently runs executables from the current directory. This flaw is due to `gitk` searching for `taskkill.exe` in the current directory before searching the `PATH`. This behavior can be exploited with social engineering to trick users into executing untrusted code. The vulnerability affects the `gitk` component and can lead to the execution of malicious code if a user runs `gitk` in a directory containing a malicious executable named `taskkill.exe`.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The vulnerable code block contains a secure coding violation related to unsafe PATH lookup. Specifically, the code originally allowed executables to be run from the current directory inadvertently, which could be exploited to execute untrusted code. This is a violation of secure coding practices because it does not ensure that only trusted executables are run, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution. The patch addresses this by overriding the `exec` and `open` commands to sanitize the command line and ensure that executables are located using a safe PATH lookup, thereby preventing the execution of untrusted code from the current directory.

mitigation.rag: A patch is available in version 2.39.2 of Git for Windows to address the vulnerability where `gitk` potentially runs executables from the current directory inadvertently. As a workaround, users are advised to avoid using `gitk` (or Git GUI's "Visualize History" functionality) in clones of untrusted repositories. The patch involves overriding the `exec` and `open` commands to avoid unsafe PATH lookups, ensuring that executables are not inadvertently run from the current directory. This mitigation does not introduce any stated limitations or side effects.

Another vulnerability involves JNDI Injection, where a remote authenticated attacker can execute arbitrary code by sending a specially crafted request using the property clientRerouteServerListJNDIName. Additionally, there is a vulnerability caused by an unchecked class instantiation when providing plugin classes, allowing a remote authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending a specially crafted request using the named pluginClassName class. IBM Db2 JDBC Driver vulnerabilities include:

This indicates a lack of proper validation and sanitization of inputs related to JNDI, which is a violation of secure coding practices as it can lead to remote code execution.

2. **Unchecked Class Instantiation**: The vulnerability allows a remote authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system due to unchecked class instantiation when providing plugin classes. This suggests a failure to validate and control the instantiation of classes, which violates secure coding principles by allowing potentially malicious classes to be instantiated.

3. **Unchecked Logger Injection**: The vulnerability allows a remote authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system, caused by an unchecked logger injection by sending a specially crafted request using the named `traceFile` property. This indicates a lack of input validation and sanitization, which is a violation of secure coding practices as it can lead to remote code execution.

- AIX Level 7.2.5: APAR IJ48252, SP07
- AIX Level 7.3.0: APAR IJ48758, N/A
- AIX Level 7.3.1: APAR IJ48540, SP03
- VIOS Level 3.1.3: APAR IJ48252, N/A
- VIOS Level 3.1.4: APAR IJ48252, 3.1.4.30

B. FIXES: IBM recommends addressing the vulnerability immediately. AIX and VIOS fixes are available and can be downloaded via HTTPS from the provided link. The fixes include prerequisite checking to ensure correct mapping with AIX Technology Levels.

C. FIX AND INTERIM FIX INSTALLATION: 

1. It is recommended to create a mksysb backup of the system and verify it is bootable and readable before proceeding.
2. To preview a fix installation, use the command: `installp -a -d fix_name -p all` where `fix_name` is the name of the fix package being previewed.
3. To install a fix package, use the command: `installp -a -d fix_name -X all` where `fix_name` is the name of the fix package being installed.
4. Interim fixes have had limited functional and regression testing but are fully supported by IBM.
5. To preview an interim fix installation, use the command: `emgr -e ipkg_name -p` where `ipkg_name` is the name of the interim fix package being previewed.
6. To install an interim fix package, use the command: `emgr -e ipkg_name -X` where `ipkg_name` is the name of the interim fix package being installed.

The mitigation steps do not mention any registry changes, Group Policy settings, security features, or services that can be disabled. There are no stated limitations or side effects of the mitigation steps in the context.

mitigation.rag:
The mitigation explicitly mentioned in the context involves disabling the ability to insert FBX files in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook for Windows and Mac. This affects Office 2019, Office 2021, Office LTSC for Mac 2021, and Microsoft 365. Additionally, as of February 13, 2024, the ability to insert FBX files has been disabled in 3D Viewer. This change is effective as of the January 9, 2024 security update. 

The limitation introduced by this mitigation is that versions of Office that previously had the feature to insert FBX files enabled will no longer have access to it. However, 3D models in Office documents that were previously inserted from an FBX file will continue to work as expected unless the Link to File option was chosen at the time of insertion.

From 2b47933fba1e9266edb1bb71163768288bbfd409 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eliah Kagan <degeneracypressure@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Dec 2023 08:54:12 -0500
Subject: [PATCH 02/16] Correct the "not from cwd" test and add more cases

This shows that CVE-2023-40590 is only partially patched. This
commit does not fix the vulnerbility, only the test.

The problem is that, when shell=True, the environment of the shell
subprocess, instead of the GitPython process, determines whether
searching for the "git" command will use the current directory.
Currently NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is set only in the
current process, and this is done after the environment for the
subprocess (env) is computed. So when git is an indirect subprocess
due to shell=True, Windows still checks a CWD when looking it up.

(Note that this should not be a problem for indirect subprocesses
started by git itself. When a standard git command is implemented
as an external executable, when git runs a custom command, and when
one git command delegates some of its work to another -- e.g.
"git clone" running git-remote-https -- Git for Windows already
does not search the current directory. Custom git commands that
start their own git subprocesses could have an analogous path
search bug, but this would be separate from the bug in GitPython.)

This is an exploitable vulnerability in GitPython. Although
shell=True is rarer and inherently less secure than the default of
shell=False, it still ought to avoid automatically running an
executable that may exist only due to having been cloned as part of
an untrusted repository. In addition, historically programs on
Windows had sometimes used shell=True as a workaround for console
windows being displayed for subprocesses, and some such code may
still be in use.

Furthermore, even when GitPython's current working directory is
outside the repository being worked on, the Git object in a Repo
instance's "git" attribute holds the repository directory as its
"_working_dir" attribute, which Git.execute consults to determine
the value of "cwd" to pass to subprocess.Popen. When the created
direct subprocess is really a shell, this is the CWD where git.exe
is looked for before searching PATH directories.

This is also why previous, more limited testing (including
accompanying manual testing with shell=True) didn't discover the
bug. Even when modified to test with shell=True, the old test had
the "impostor" git.exe in the GitPython process's own current
directory (which was changed to a temporary directory for the test,
where the "impostor" was created, but this was separate from the
working tree of the self.git repository). This was effective for
the shell=False case, but not the shell=True case where the
impostor would be found and run in the repository directory even
when it differs from the GitPython process's CWD.

From: Eliah Kagan <degeneracypressure@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Dec 2023 18:35:01 -0500
Subject: [PATCH 08/16] Start on test_hook_uses_shell_not_from_cwd

This shows that run_commit_hook is vulnerable to an untrusted
search path bug on Windows, when running script hooks: bash.exe is
run without setting NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath or otherwise
excluding the current directory from the path search.

The new test uses a non-bare repo, even though the surrounding
tests use bare repos. Although the test also works if the repo is
initialized with `Repo.init(rw_dir, bare=True)`, using a bare repo
would obscure how the bug this test reveals would typically be
exploited, where a command that uses a hook is run after a
malicious bash.exe is checked out into the working tree from an
untrusted branch.

Running hooks that are themselves provided by an untrusted
repository or branch is of course never safe. If an attacker can
deceive a user into doing that, then this vulnerability is not
needed. Instead, an attack that leverages this untrusted search
path vulnerability would most likely be of roughly this form:

1. The user clones a trusted repository and installs hooks.
2. A malicious party offers a contribution to the project.
3. The user checks out the malicious party's untrusted branch.
4. The user performs an action that runs a hook.

The hook the user runs is still trusted, but it runs with the
malicious bash.exe found in the current directory (which is the
working tree or perhaps some subdirectory of it).

The test added in this commit should, if possible, be improved to
be able to run and detect the bug (or its absence) even when bash
is absent from the Windows system and, preferably, also even when
the WSL bash.exe is present but no WSL distribution is installed.

+class VirtualEnvironment:
+    """A newly created Python virtual environment for use in a test."""
+
+    __slots__ = ("_env_dir",)
+
+    def __init__(self, env_dir, *, with_pip):
+        self._env_dir = env_dir
+        venv.create(env_dir, symlinks=(os.name != "nt"), with_pip=with_pip)
+
+    @property
+    def env_dir(self):
+        """The top-level directory of the environment."""

+    @property

+    @property

+        return os.path.join(self.env_dir, "src")

From f44524a9a9c8122b9b98d6e5797e1dfc3211c0b7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eliah Kagan <degeneracypressure@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Dec 2023 08:11:04 +0800
Subject: [PATCH 12/16] Avoid spurious "location may have moved" on Windows

The main case where this happens is when tempfile.gettempdir() has
a component in it that uses an 8.3-encoded path, e.g.,
C:\Users\Administrator\... -> C:\Users\ADMINI~1\...

This is a workaround for python/cpython#90329. I call realpath only
once, when the venv is created, and not on any paths inside the
venv, to make it less likely this masks the problems the warning is
meant for. (For example, if Scripts, or python.exe in it, produced
this even with the venv created as it is now, then that may indicte
an actual problem.)

Note that copying python.exe from Scripts to one level up in the
venv, and changing its name to bash.exe to use it to simulate the
bash.exe impostor, as is done in test_hook_uses_shell_not_from_cwd,
should not (and does not) produce this warning. If that ever starts
to do so, then that should be examined as a sign of brittleness.

From c551e916c7b9e2d623b9d76f3352849a707d9bbe Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eliah Kagan <degeneracypressure@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Dec 2023 00:40:43 -0500
Subject: [PATCH 14/16] Extract shared logic for using Popen safely on Windows

This creates git.util.safer_popen that, on non-Windows systems, is
bound to subprocess.Popen (to avoid introducing unnecessary
latency). On Windows, it is a function that wraps subprocess.Popen,
consolidating two pieces of logic that had previously been
duplicated:

1. Temporarily setting NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath in the
   calling environment and, when shell=True is used, setting it in
   the subprocess environment as well. This prevents executables
   specified as single names (which are mainly "git" and, for
   hooks, "bash.exe") from being searched for in the current
   working directory of GitPython or, when a shell is used, the
   current working directory of the shell used to run them.

2. Passing the CREATE_NO_WINDOW and CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP flags
   as creationflags. This is not a security measure. It is
   indirectly related to safety in that CREATE_NO_WINDOW eliminated
   at least some, and possibly all, cases where calling Git.execute
   (directly, or indirectly via a dynamic method) with shell=True
   conferred an advantage over the inherently more secure default
   of shell=False; and CREATE_NEW_PROCESS facilitates some ways of
   terminating subprocesses that would otherwise be unavailable,
   thereby making resource exhaustion less likely. But really the
   reason I included creationflags here is that it seems it should
   always be used in the same situations as preventing the current
   directory from being searched (and always was), and including it
   further reduces code duplication and simplifies calling code.

This commit does not improve security or robustness, because these
features were already present. Instead, this moves them to a single
location. It also documents them by giving the function bound to
safer_popen on Windows, _safer_popen_windows, a detailed docstring.

Because there would otherwise be potential for confusion on the
different ways to perform or customize path searches, I have also
added a doctring to py_where noting its limited use case and its
relationship to shutil.which and non-shell search.

(The search in _safer_popen_windows is typically a non-shell
search, which is why it cannot be reimplemented to do its own
lookup by calling an only slightly modified version of
shutil.which, without a risk of breaking some currently working
uses. It may, however, be possible to fix the race condition by
doing something analogous for Windows non-shell search behavior,
which is largely but not entirely described in the documentation
for CreateProcessW.)

From 3eb7c2ab82e6dbe101ff916fca29d539cc2793af Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eliah Kagan <degeneracypressure@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Dec 2023 03:48:53 -0500
Subject: [PATCH 15/16] Move safer_popen from git.util to git.cmd

I had originally written it in git.util because it is used from two
separate modules (git.cmd and git.index.fun) and is arguably the
same sort of thing as remove_password_if_present, in that both
relate to running processes (and to security) and both are used
from multiple modules yet are not meant for use outside GitPython.

However, all of this is also true of git.cmd.handle_process_output,
which this really has more in common with: it's a utility related
*only* to the use of subprocesses, while remove_password_if_present
can be used for other sanitization. In addition, it also replaces
git.cmd.PROC_CREATIONFLAGS (also imported in git.index.fun) by
passing that to Popen on Windows (since the situations where a
custom value of creationflags should be used are the same as those
where safer_popen should be called for its primary benefit of
avoiding an untrusted path search when creating the subprocess).

safer_popen and its Windows implementation _safer_popen_windows are
thus moved from git/util.py to git/cmd.py, with related changes,
such as to imports, done everywhere they are needed.

+    env: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
+    **kwargs: Any,
+) -> Popen:
+    """Call :class:`subprocess.Popen` on Windows but don't include a CWD in the search.
+
+    This avoids an untrusted search path condition where a file like ``git.exe`` in a
+    malicious repository would be run when GitPython operates on the repository. The
+    process using GitPython may have an untrusted repository's working tree as its
+    current working directory. Some operations may temporarily change to that directory
+    before running a subprocess. In addition, while by default GitPython does not run
+    external commands with a shell, it can be made to do so, in which case the CWD of
+    the subprocess, which GitPython usually sets to a repository working tree, can
+    itself be searched automatically by the shell. This wrapper covers all those cases.
+
+    :note: This currently works by setting the ``NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath``
+        environment variable during subprocess creation. It also takes care of passing
+        Windows-specific process creation flags, but that is unrelated to path search.
+
+    :note: The current implementation contains a race condition on :attr:`os.environ`.
+        GitPython isn't thread-safe, but a program using it on one thread should ideally
+        be able to mutate :attr:`os.environ` on another, without unpredictable results.
+        See comments in https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/pull/1650.
+    """
+    # CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP is needed for some ways of killing it afterwards. See:
+    # https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.Popen.send_signal
+    # https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP
+    creationflags = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW | subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP
+
+    # When using a shell, the shell is the direct subprocess, so the variable must be
+    # set in its environment, to affect its search behavior. (The "1" can be any value.)
+    if shell:

+        safer_env["NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath"] = "1"
+    else:
+        safer_env = env
+
+    # When not using a shell, the current process does the search in a CreateProcessW
+    # API call, so the variable must be set in our environment. With a shell, this is
+    # unnecessary, in versions where https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/101283 is
+    # patched. If not, in the rare case the ComSpec environment variable is unset, the
+    # shell is searched for unsafely. Setting NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath in all
+    # cases, as here, is simpler and protects against that. (The "1" can be any value.)
+    with patch_env("NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath", "1"):

+            command,
+            shell=shell,
+            env=safer_env,
+            creationflags=creationflags,
+            **kwargs,
+        )

exploit_steps.rag:
1. **Environment or Setup Needed:**
   - The user must clone a trusted repository and install hooks.
   - A malicious party must offer a contribution to the project.
   - The user must check out the malicious party's untrusted branch.
   - The environment should be such that `bash.exe` or a similar executable is present in the current directory, which is the working tree or a subdirectory of it.

2. **Input Format or Payload Used:**
   - The malicious branch should contain a `bash.exe` or similar executable that the attacker wants to run.

3. **Functions or Files Involved in Triggering the Vulnerability:**
   - The vulnerability is triggered when the user performs an action that runs a hook.
   - The hook is trusted but runs with the malicious `bash.exe` found in the current directory.

4. **Expected Behavior that Confirms Successful Exploitation:**
   - The trusted hook runs, but it executes the malicious `bash.exe` from the current directory instead of the intended executable.
   - The presence of a side effect, such as a file being created or modified, can confirm that the impostor `bash.exe` was executed. For example, the output "ran fake hook" being written to `output.txt` indicates the hook was executed.

remote_exploitability.rag: The access vector is "LOCAL," which means the attacker needs direct access to the system. There is no indication in the context that this vulnerability can be triggered remotely.

root_cause.rag: GitPython has a vulnerability related to an untrusted search path on Windows. The root cause is that when GitPython uses `bash.exe` to run hooks, it does not prevent finding and executing `bash.exe` from the current directory, which could be the working tree of an untrusted repository. This issue arises because the `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` is not set, allowing a malicious `bash.exe` to be executed if present in the current directory. This vulnerability is particularly exploitable in workflows where a branch from an untrusted remote is checked out for review, potentially containing a malicious `bash.exe`.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The violation of secure coding practices identified in the context is related to the untrusted search path vulnerability in GitPython. Specifically, when GitPython uses `bash.exe` to run hooks, it does not prevent the executable from being found and run in the current directory, which may be the working tree of an untrusted repository. This is a violation because it allows a malicious `bash.exe` to be executed if it is present in the current directory, potentially leading to exploitation. The vulnerability arises from not setting `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` or otherwise excluding the current directory from the path search, which is a failure to implement proper validation and control over executable search paths.

patch_expl.rag: The vulnerability was addressed in the commit with ID 91641c4da0a011d4c5352e88fc68389d4e1289a5, which modifies the Vite dev server to handle case-insensitive file systems correctly. The change involves updating the `picomatch` configuration in the `vite/src/node/server/index.ts` file to include the `nocase: true` option, ensuring that the `server.fs.deny` option properly blocks access to sensitive files regardless of case variations. This fix is included in the Vite versions vite@5.0.12, vite@4.5.2, vite@3.2.8, and vite@2.9.17.

exploit_steps.rag:
**Setup:**

1. Create a vanilla Vite project using the command `npm create vite@latest` on a Standard Azure hosted Windows 10 instance.
2. Run the development server with the command `npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0`, making it publicly accessible at `http://20.12.242.81:5173/`.
3. Create dummy secret files, such as `custom.secret` and `production.pem`.
4. Populate the `vite.config.js` file with the following configuration:
   ```javascript
   export default { server: { fs: { deny: ['.env', '.env.*', '*.{crt,pem}', 'custom.secret'] } } }
   ```

**Reproduction:**

1. Use the command `curl -s http://20.12.242.81:5173/@fs//` to access the server. This will reveal a descriptive error page that exposes the absolute filesystem path to the project root.
2. Execute the command `curl -s http://20.12.242.81:5173/@fs/C:/Users/darbonzo/Desktop/vite-project/vite.config.js` to access the configuration file. This file reveals the locations of secrets.
3. Use the command `curl -s http://20.12.242.81:5173/@fs/C:/Users/darbonzo/Desktop/vite-project/custom.sEcReT` to access secrets directly. This is possible by using a case-augmented version of the filename.

**Expected Behavior:**

- The descriptive error page should reveal the absolute filesystem path to the project root.
- The configuration file should be accessible, revealing the locations of secrets.
- Secrets should be directly accessible using case-augmented versions of filenames, confirming the bypass of the `server.fs.deny` configuration.

root_cause.rag: The Vite dev server option `server.fs.deny` can be bypassed on case-insensitive file systems using case-augmented versions of filenames. This vulnerability is caused by the default behavior of `picomatch`, which uses case-sensitive glob matching, while the file server does not discriminate based on case. As a result, the matcher derived from `config.server.fs.deny` fails to block access to sensitive files when raw filesystem paths are requested with augmented casing. This issue notably affects servers hosted on Windows, where the file system is case-insensitive. The potential impact includes the discovery and accessibility of files that should be protected by `server.fs.deny`.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The violation of secure coding practices found in the vulnerable code block is related to the bypass of the `server.fs.deny` option on case-insensitive file systems. The issue arises because the file server does not discriminate based on case, allowing a blacklist bypass by using case-augmented versions of filenames. This means that files intended to be protected by `server.fs.deny` can be accessed if the filenames are requested with different casing. This is a violation of secure coding practices as it allows unauthorized access to sensitive files, such as configuration files and secrets, due to improper handling of case sensitivity in file path matching.

mitigation.rag: Fixed in vite@5.0.12, vite@4.5.2, vite@3.2.8, vite@2.9.17. Users are advised to upgrade. Users unable to upgrade should restrict access to dev servers.

patch_expl.rag: The patch is identified by the Git commit ID 8f4acff3c2d45c1cb07779bb3fe79644408ee387. It addresses a vulnerability in the electron-builder's NSIS installer script by modifying the way system commands are executed. The change involves executing `%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\cmd.exe` directly instead of relying on the default behavior of NSExec, which previously searched the current directory before the system `PATH`. This update prevents the execution of a malicious `cmd.exe` if placed in the same directory as the installer. The fix is applied in version 24.13.2 of electron-builder.

exploited_versions.rag: Not found

exploit_steps.rag:
To successfully exploit the vulnerability described, the following steps are required:

1. **Environment or Setup Needed:**
   - The vulnerability affects the NSIS installer of electron-builder versions prior to 24.13.2 on Windows systems.

2. **Input Format or Payload Used:**
   - An attacker needs to place a malicious executable file named `cmd.exe` in the same directory as the installer.

3. **Functions or Files Involved in Triggering the Vulnerability:**
   - The NSIS installer script uses `NSExec` to make a system call to open `cmd.exe`. By default, `NSExec` searches the current directory of the installer before searching the system `PATH`.

4. **Expected Behavior that Confirms Successful Exploitation:**
   - If the malicious `cmd.exe` is executed instead of the legitimate system `cmd.exe`, it indicates successful exploitation of the vulnerability. The installer will run the malicious file, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary code at the installer level.

remote_exploitability.rag: The access vector is "LOCAL," which means the attacker needs direct access to the system. The vulnerability is not remotely exploitable as it requires the attacker to place a malicious executable file named cmd.exe in the same folder as the installer, indicating local access is necessary.

root_cause.rag: A vulnerability exists in electron-builder versions prior to 24.13.2 for Windows, where the NSIS installer makes a system call to open cmd.exe via NSExec in the `.nsh` installer script. The root cause of the vulnerability is that NSExec by default searches the current directory of where the installer is located before searching the `PATH`. This flaw allows an attacker to place a malicious executable file named cmd.exe in the same folder as the installer, causing the installer to execute the malicious file instead of the legitimate cmd.exe. The vulnerability affects the installer-level execution before the app is present on the system, leading to potential execution of arbitrary code with the privileges of the installer process.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The vulnerable code block in the NSIS installer script makes a system call to open `cmd.exe` via `nsExec`. The violation of secure coding practices here is that `nsExec` by default searches the current directory of where the installer is located before searching the `PATH`. This behavior allows an attacker to place a malicious executable file named `cmd.exe` in the same folder as the installer, which would then be executed instead of the intended system `cmd.exe`. This constitutes a violation of secure coding practices as it allows for potential execution of malicious code due to improper handling of executable paths, leading to a security vulnerability.

mitigation.rag: Version 24.13.2 of electron-builder fixes the vulnerability by executing `%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\cmd.exe` directly during the NSIS installer process. This change ensures that the system's cmd.exe is used instead of any potentially malicious executable named cmd.exe placed in the same directory as the installer. No known workaround exists for versions prior to 24.13.2. The mitigation does not introduce any stated limitations or side effects.

This allows the malicious cmd.exe to be executed instead of the legitimate system cmd.exe, potentially leading to unauthorized code execution at the installer level.

root_cause.rag: Mio is a Metal I/O library for Rust. When using named pipes on Windows, mio will under some circumstances return invalid tokens that correspond to named pipes that have already been deregistered from the mio registry. This vulnerability is Windows-specific and can only happen if you are using named pipes. The impact of this vulnerability depends on how mio is used. For some applications, invalid tokens may be ignored or cause a warning or a crash. However, for applications that store pointers in the tokens, this vulnerability may result in a use-after-free. For users of Tokio, this vulnerability is serious and can result in a use-after-free in Tokio. The vulnerability affects all versions of mio between v0.7.2 and v0.8.10, and Tokio is vulnerable when using a vulnerable version of mio and at least Tokio v1.30.0. Versions of Tokio prior to v1.30.0 will ignore invalid tokens, so they are not vulnerable.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The vulnerable code block contains a potential secure programming violation related to the handling of invalid tokens in the context of named pipes on Windows. Specifically, the code may return invalid tokens that correspond to named pipes that have already been deregistered from the mio registry. This can lead to a use-after-free vulnerability, particularly in applications that store pointers in the tokens. The violation is due to the lack of proper validation and handling of these tokens, which can result in serious security issues such as application crashes or unintended behavior.

mitigation.rag: The mitigation explicitly mentioned in the context is the update to mio version v0.8.11, which fixes the vulnerability. All versions of mio between v0.7.2 and v0.8.10 are vulnerable. Versions of Tokio prior to v1.30.0 will ignore invalid tokens, so they are not vulnerable. Vulnerable libraries that use mio can work around this issue by detecting and ignoring invalid tokens. Patch code.rag:
```diff
+ Read secure_version under sha256 protection
+ 
+ First check has been added in the bootloader to ensure correct secure
+ version after application verification and loading stage. This check
+ happens before setting up the flash cache mapping and handling over
+ the final control to application. This check ensures that application
+ was not swapped (e.g., to lower security version but valid image) just
+ before the load stage in bootloader.
+ 
+ Second check has been added in the application startup code to ensure
+ that currently booting app has higher security version than the one
+ programmed in the eFuse for anti-rollback scenario. This will ensure
+ that only the legit application boots-up on the device for
+ anti-rollback case.
```

patch_expl.rag:
The patch with commit ID 3305cb4d235182067936f8e940e6db174e25b4b2 addresses additional checks for the secure version in the anti-rollback case. This change was necessary to prevent attempts to boot a lower security version but valid application, such as a passive partition image. The patch ensures that the secure version is read under sha256 protection and includes a check in the bootloader to verify the correct secure version after application verification and loading stage. This check occurs before setting up the flash cache mapping and handing over control to the application, ensuring that the application was not swapped to a lower security version just before the load stage in the bootloader.

The patch with commit ID f327ddf6adab0c28d395975785727b2feef57803 merges the branch 'bugfix/ota_anti_rollback_checks_2_v4.4' into 'release/v4.4'. It includes the feature to read the secure version under sha256 protection for version 4.4.

The patch with commit ID c33b9e1426121ce8cccf1a94241740be9cff68de fixes the bootloader support by checking the secure version only for the application image. This change was necessary because the secure version in the image header is only available for the application image, and the bootloader should not verify its own image for the secure version. This resolves a regression introduced in a previous commit (3305cb4d).

The patch with commit ID 7003f1ef0dffc73c34eb153d1b0710babb078149 merges the branch 'bugfix/ota_anti_rollback_checks_2_v5.1' into 'release/v5.1'. It includes the feature to read the secure version under sha256 protection for version 5.1.

1. **Environment or Setup Needed:**
   - The attacker must have physical access to the device's flash memory.
   - The device must be running a vulnerable version of the ESP-IDF bootloader, specifically versions 4.4.6, 5.0.6, 5.1.3, or 5.2.

2. **Input Format or Payload Used:**
   - The attack involves modifying the flash contents of the device. This modification must occur after the anti-rollback checks have been performed by the bootloader but before the application is loaded.

3. **Functions or Files Involved in Triggering the Vulnerability:**
   - The vulnerability is related to the implementation of the ESP-IDF bootloader, specifically in the handling of the `esp_app_desc_t` structure and the `secure_version` field.
   - The function `esp_efuse_check_secure_version` is involved in checking the secure version.
   - The file `esp_image_format.c` contains logic related to processing segment data, where anti-rollback checks are performed.

4. **Expected Behavior that Confirms Successful Exploitation:**
   - Successful exploitation allows the attacker to bypass the anti-rollback protection, enabling the booting of an application partition with a lower security version than the one programmed in the eFuse of the chip.
   - The attack is confirmed successful if the device boots an application with a lower security version despite the presence of flash encryption and anti-rollback mechanisms.

root_cause.rag: A Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) vulnerability exists in the implementation of the ESP-IDF bootloader. This vulnerability allows an attacker with physical access to the device's flash to bypass anti-rollback protection. The anti-rollback mechanism is designed to prevent reverting to an application with a security version lower than the one programmed in the chip's eFuse. The vulnerability arises because the attacker can modify the flash contents after the bootloader has performed anti-rollback checks but before the application is loaded. This flaw allows booting an application partition with a lower security version, even when a flash encryption scheme is in place.

The context does not provide explicit step-by-step instructions or actions required to successfully exploit the vulnerability described. However, the following technical details are available:

- **Environment or Setup Needed**: The vulnerability is related to the Linux kernel, specifically affecting the powerpc/pseries architecture with IOMMU table initialization for kdump over SR-IOV. The kernel version mentioned is 6.4.0-Test102+ on IBM POWER10 hardware.

- **Functions or Files Involved**: The vulnerability involves the IOMMU table initialization process. Functions mentioned in the context include `iommu_area_alloc()`, `iommu_range_alloc()`, `iommu_alloc()`, `iommu_alloc_coherent()`, `dma_iommu_alloc_coherent()`, `dma_alloc_attrs()`, and several functions related to the mlx5_core module.

- **Expected Behavior that Confirms Successful Exploitation**: The context describes a scenario where a NULL pointer exception occurs, leading to a kernel panic when the kdump kernel tries to copy dump data over SR-IOV. This is due to the IOMMU table not being initialized correctly, resulting in a NULL pointer dereference when the device driver attempts to enter TCEs for the SR-IOV device.

No specific input format or payload used to trigger the vulnerability is provided in the context.

root_cause.rag: In the Linux kernel, a vulnerability exists where the IOMMU table is not initialized for kdump over SR-IOV. This issue arises when the kdump kernel attempts to copy dump data over SR-IOV, leading to a NULL pointer exception and causing the LPAR to panic. The root cause is that the IOMMU table is not initialized when TCEs (Translation Control Entries) are dynamically allocated for SR-IOV, as the function `iommu_table_setparms_lpar()` only considers the "ibm,dma-window" property. Consequently, when the device driver tries to enter TCEs for the SR-IOV device, a NULL pointer exception is thrown from `iommu_area_alloc()`. This vulnerability affects the initialization process of PCI busses and IOMMU group/tables in `pci_dma_bus_setup_pSeriesLP()`, specifically in scenarios where the "ibm,dma-window" is absent.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The violation of secure coding practices identified in the context is related to the improper initialization of the IOMMU table for kdump over SR-IOV in the Linux kernel. Specifically, the issue arises when the kdump kernel attempts to copy dump data over SR-IOV, leading to a NULL pointer exception. This occurs because the IOMMU table is not initialized when TCEs (Translation Control Entries) are dynamically allocated for SR-IOV. The function `iommu_table_setparms_lpar()` only considers the "ibm,dma-window" property when initializing the IOMMU table. In scenarios where the default DMA window is removed and DDW (Dynamic DMA Windows) are added, the newly created IOMMU table is not initialized, resulting in a NULL pointer exception when the device driver tries to enter TCEs for the SR-IOV device. This reflects a violation of secure coding practices due to missing validation and incorrect error handling, leading to potential system instability and security vulnerabilities.

mitigation.rag:
Initialize the IOMMU table with the DDW property stored in the FDT. For the dedicated adapter, the kdump kernel would encounter both default and DDW in FDT, and the DDW property is used to initialize the IOMMU table. A DDW could be direct or dynamic mapped. The kdump kernel would initialize the IOMMU table and mark the existing DDW as "dynamic." This works fine since, at the time of table initialization, `iommu_table_clear()` makes some space in the DDW for a predefined number of TCEs needed for kdump to succeed. 

At the time of LPAR dump, before kexec hands over control to the kdump kernel, DDWs are scanned and added to the FDT. For the SR-IOV case, the default DMA window "ibm,dma-window" is removed from the FDT and DDW added for the device. When the kdump kernel initializes, PCI busses are scanned, and IOMMU group/tables are created in `pci_dma_bus_setup_pSeriesLP()`. For the SR-IOV case, there is no "ibm,dma-window." The original commit fixes the path where memory is pre-mapped (direct mapped) to the DDW. When TCEs are direct mapped, there is no need to initialize IOMMU tables. 

`iommu_table_setparms_lpar()` only considers the "ibm,dma-window" property when initializing the IOMMU table. In the scenario where TCEs are dynamically allocated for SR-IOV, the newly created IOMMU table is not initialized. Later, when the device driver tries to enter TCEs for the SR-IOV device, a NULL pointer exception is thrown from `iommu_area_alloc()`. 

No registry changes, Group Policy settings, security features, or services that can be disabled are mentioned. No commands, registry keys, or scripts are specified. The mitigation steps are stated to be complete.

patch_expl.rag: The SSRF vulnerability was addressed in the commit with ID 43bb71d115d78c03faa82d75445dd908e9b32716. This patch was necessary to prevent the server from making unauthorized connections to internal-only services within the organization’s infrastructure when a malicious app is uploaded to the Static analyzer. The fix was applied in version 3.9.8 of the Mobile Security Framework (MobSF). The patch involved changes to the files `mobsf/MobSF/init.py`, `views/common/shared_func.py`, `poetry.lock`, and `pyproject.toml`. The advisory related to this fix is GHSA-wpff-wm84-x5cx.

root_cause.rag: A SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) vulnerability exists in the firebase database check logic of the Mobile Security Framework (MobSF). This vulnerability allows an attacker to cause the server to make a connection to internal-only services within the organization’s infrastructure. The issue arises when a malicious app is uploaded to the Static Analyzer, enabling the possibility of making internal requests. This vulnerability affects the MobSF version prior to 3.9.8.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The vulnerable code block contains a violation of secure coding practices related to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The original code allowed for potential SSRF by not adequately validating the Firebase URL, which could enable an attacker to make the server initiate requests to internal-only services within the organization's infrastructure. The patch addresses this by adding a check to ensure that the URL ends with 'firebaseio.com' and by setting `allow_redirects=False` in the `requests.get` call to prevent automatic redirection, which could be exploited in SSRF attacks.

This change was essential to prevent the execution of remote code by ensuring that commands are correctly quoted, thereby mitigating the risk of command injection. The patch is documented in the security advisory GHSA-42h4-v29r-42qg on GitHub.

root_cause.rag: A vulnerability exists in the yt-dlp project where the shell escape function improperly handles command execution when using the `--exec` option with `%q` on Windows. The root cause of this vulnerability is the inadequate escaping of double quotes, which allows for the expansion of environment variables. This flaw can lead to remote code execution (RCE) when commands are improperly quoted, allowing special characters to be executed. The issue affects the `utils.Popen` function, which was initially patched to replace double quotes with two double quotes, but this was insufficient to prevent the vulnerability.

secure_coding_violation.rag:
The vulnerable code block in the provided context is related to the improper handling of shell command execution in the `yt-dlp` project, specifically when using the `--exec` option with `%q` on Windows. The secure coding violation identified is:

The shell escape function used in the code does not adequately escape special characters, particularly the `%` character. This allows for command injection through the expansion of environment variables. The `%CMDCMDLINE%` variable can be manipulated to unbalance quotes, leading to the execution of unintended commands. This is a violation of secure coding practices as it fails to properly validate and sanitize input before executing it in a shell context, which is inherently dangerous and can lead to remote code execution (RCE). The patch addresses this by properly escaping `%`, `\`, and `\n` to prevent such vulnerabilities.

mitigation.rag:
The mitigation steps explicitly mentioned in the context are as follows:

1. Upgrade yt-dlp to version 2024.04.09 to address the vulnerability. This version includes a fix that properly escapes `%` by replacing them with `%%cd:~,%`, which expands to nothing, leaving only the leading percent.

2. For Windows users who are not able to upgrade, it is recommended to avoid using any output template expansion in `--exec` other than `{}` (filepath). If expansion in `--exec` is needed, verify that the fields used do not contain `"`, `|`, or `&`. Alternatively, instead of using `--exec`, write the info json and load the fields from it instead.

patch_expl.rag: The patch addresses critical security issues in the GLPI Agent's Windows MSI packaging. The commit ID for this patch is 41bbb1169e899bd15350a9e2fdbf9269a3b7a14f. The patch includes changes to the `contrib/windows/packaging/MSI_main-v2.wxs.tt` file, adding error handling and custom actions to ensure only administrators can modify the installation. This update is necessary to prevent local users from modifying the GLPI Agent configuration to gain higher privileges, as indicated by the CVE-2024-28240 and CVE-2024-28241 advisories. The patch is part of the GLPI-Agent version 1.7.2 release.

exploit_steps.rag:
The vulnerability described affects the GLPI-Agent installed on Windows via MSI packaging. To exploit this vulnerability, the following steps are required:

1. **Environment Setup:**
   - The GLPI-Agent must be installed on a Windows system using MSI packaging.
   - The Deploy task must be installed on the system.

2. **Exploitation Steps:**
   - A local user must have access to the system where the GLPI-Agent is installed.
   - The user can modify the GLPI-Agent configuration to replace the GLPI server URL with an incorrect URL or disable the service entirely, causing a denial of service.
   - If the Deploy task is installed, a local malicious user can configure a malicious server to provide its own deploy task payload, potentially leading to privilege escalation.

3. **Files and Functions Involved:**
   - The GLPI-Agent configuration files are involved, specifically those that define the server URL and deploy task settings.

4. **Expected Behavior:**
   - Successful exploitation would result in the GLPI-Agent being unable to connect to the correct server, leading to a denial of service.
   - In the case of privilege escalation, the malicious payload from the configured server would execute with elevated privileges.

No additional technical details, such as specific input formats or payloads, are provided in the context.

remote_exploitability.rag: The access vector is "LOCAL," which means the attacker needs direct access to the system. The context indicates that the vulnerability can be exploited by a local user to cause denial of service or privilege escalation, confirming that it is not remotely exploitable.

root_cause.rag: A vulnerability exists in the GLPI Agent installed on Windows via MSI packaging, where a local user can cause a denial of service by replacing the GLPI server URL with an incorrect one or disabling the service. Additionally, if the Deploy task is installed, a local malicious user can escalate privileges by configuring a malicious server to provide its own deploy task payload. This vulnerability affects the GLPI-Agent and is related to its configuration, allowing unauthorized modifications that can lead to privilege escalation.

secure_coding_violation.rag: A secure coding violation is identified in the GLPI Agent's MSI packaging for Windows. The vulnerability allows a local user to modify the GLPI-Agent installation or configuration to gain higher privileges. Specifically, the violation involves insufficient validation of user privileges during the installation or configuration process, which can lead to privilege escalation. The patch addresses this by adding checks to ensure that only administrators can modify the installation, as indicated by the addition of the error message "Only administrators can modify [AgentName] installation" and the implementation of custom actions to verify administrative privileges during the installation process.

mitigation.rag: Edit the GLPI-Agent related key under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall` and add `SystemComponent` DWORD value setting it to `1` to hide GLPI-Agent from installed applications. This is a workaround for the vulnerability. No limitations or side effects are mentioned in the context.

exploit_steps.rag:
1. **Environment Setup:**
   - Ensure you are operating in a Windows environment where PHP is installed.
   - The PHP version should be one of the affected versions: 8.1.* before 8.1.28, 8.2.* before 8.2.18, or 8.3.* before 8.3.5.

2. **Create a Batch File:**
   - Save the following content into a file named `test.bat`:
     ```batch
     echo hello
     ```

3. **Create a PHP Script:**
   - Save the following PHP code into a file named `test.php`:
     ```php
     <?php
     $descriptorspec = [STDIN, STDOUT, STDOUT];
     $proc = proc_open(["test.bat", "\"&notepad.exe"], $descriptorspec, $pipes);
     proc_close($proc);
     ```

4. **Execute the PHP Script:**
   - Run the `test.php` script using PHP.

5. **Confirm Exploitation:**
   - Successful exploitation is confirmed if `notepad.exe` is executed upon running the PHP script.

6. **Alternative Confirmation:**
   - To confirm that the `bypass_shell` option does not prevent this behavior, modify the PHP script as follows and execute it:
     ```php
     <?php
     $descriptorspec = [STDIN, STDOUT, STDOUT];
     $proc = proc_open(["test.bat", "\"&notepad.exe"], $descriptorspec, $pipes, null, null, array("bypass_shell" => true));
     proc_close($proc);
     ```
   - Again, successful exploitation is confirmed if `notepad.exe` is executed.

remote_exploitability.rag: The access vector is "NETWORK," indicating that the vulnerability can be exploited over a network connection. The context supports this by describing the vulnerability as allowing arbitrary command execution via command line arguments passed to `.bat` or `.cmd` files through `proc_open`, which can be triggered remotely.

root_cause.rag: A vulnerability exists in PHP versions 8.1.* before 8.1.28, 8.2.* before 8.2.18, and 8.3.* before 8.3.5, where the `proc_open()` command with array syntax does not sufficiently escape command line arguments. This improper handling allows maliciously crafted arguments to inject arbitrary commands when executing `.bat` or `.cmd` files on Windows, even if the `bypass_shell` option is enabled. The vulnerability arises because `CreateProcess` implicitly spawns `cmd.exe`, causing command line arguments to be parsed in `cmd.exe`, contrary to the documentation's claim that it doesn't spawn the shell. This flaw can lead to unexpected code execution, as command line arguments are not expected to be parsed via the shell.

secure_coding_violation.rag:
The violation of secure coding practices in the provided code block is due to improper handling of command line arguments in the `proc_open` function when used with array syntax on Windows. Specifically, the issue arises because:

1. **Insufficient Escaping**: The `proc_open` function, when used with array syntax, does not adequately escape command line arguments. This allows a malicious user to supply arguments that can execute arbitrary commands in the Windows shell.

2. **Unexpected Shell Invocation**: Despite the `bypass_shell` option being enabled, executing `.bat` or `.cmd` files results in `CreateProcess` implicitly spawning `cmd.exe`. This behavior contradicts the documentation, which states that the shell should not be spawned, leading to command line arguments being parsed by `cmd.exe`.

3. **Command Injection**: The improper handling and escaping of arguments allow for command injection. For example, the argument `["test.bat", "\"&notepad.exe"]` can lead to the execution of `notepad.exe`, demonstrating the vulnerability to arbitrary command execution.

These issues collectively violate secure coding principles by allowing unauthorized command execution through insufficient input validation and escaping, leading to potential security risks.

exploit_expl.rag: Malicious command line arguments can be used to execute arbitrary commands when passed to `.bat` or `.cmd` files through the `proc_open` function in PHP. This occurs even if the `bypass_shell` option is enabled, due to improper handling of command line arguments on Windows. The vulnerability is exploited by crafting arguments that inject arbitrary commands, which are then executed by `cmd.exe` because `CreateProcess` implicitly spawns `cmd.exe` when executing batch files. For example, using the command `test.bat "\"&calc.exe"` will result in `calc.exe` being executed. This method allows unexpected code execution by leveraging the fact that command line arguments are parsed in `cmd.exe`, despite the documentation stating otherwise.

patch_expl.rag: The patch titled "Quote the path to sunshinesvc.exe when launching the termination helper" was applied to address an issue where the path to sunshinesvc.exe needed to be quoted to prevent `CreateProcess()` from running `C:\Program.exe` if it was present. This change was necessary because the presence of spaces in the path could lead to incorrect execution. The patch was merged into the repository and is associated with the pull request URL: https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/2379. exploited_versions.rag: Windows versions affected by this vulnerability are those running Sunshine versions 0.17.0 through 0.22.2 as a service.

exploit_steps.rag:
The vulnerability described involves the potential execution of unintended programs due to unquoted paths in the `CreateProcess()` function call. Here are the step-by-step instructions or actions required to exploit this vulnerability:

1. **Environment Setup:**
   - The vulnerability is present in Sunshine versions 0.17.0 through 0.22.2 running as a service on Windows.
   - The system must have manually loosened ACLs (Access Control Lists) on the system drive, specifically on the `C:\` directory, to allow ordinary user writes.

2. **Input Format or Payload:**
   - Place a file named `C:\Program.exe`, `C:\Program.bat`, or `C:\Program.cmd` on the user's computer. This file should contain the payload or code intended to be executed.

3. **Functions or Files Involved:**
   - The vulnerability is triggered by the `CreateProcess()` function call in the `tools/sunshinesvc.cpp` file. The path to `sunshinesvc.exe` needs to be quoted to prevent this issue.

4. **Expected Behavior:**
   - If the path is not quoted and the conditions are met (i.e., the presence of `C:\Program.exe` and loosened ACLs), `CreateProcess()` will execute `C:\Program.exe` instead of the intended executable.
   - Successful exploitation is confirmed if `C:\Program.exe` is executed when the service attempts to run the termination helper.

Note: The vulnerability is not exploitable unless the user has manually loosened ACLs on the system drive, and the system locale may affect the name of the executable.

remote_exploitability.rag: The vulnerability is not remotely exploitable. The CVSS v3 access vector indicates "PHYSICAL," meaning the attacker requires physical access to the system. Additionally, the context specifies that the attack vector isn't exploitable unless the user has manually loosened ACLs on the system drive, further indicating that remote exploitation is not feasible.

root_cause.rag: A vulnerability exists due to the failure to quote the path to `sunshinesvc.exe` when launching the termination helper. This oversight can lead to `CreateProcess()` executing `C:\Program.exe` if it is present, rather than the intended executable. The vulnerability is contingent upon the presence of a file named `C:\Program.exe`, `C:\Program.bat`, or `C:\Program.cmd` on the user's computer, and it is not exploitable unless the user has manually loosened ACLs on the system drive. The affected component is the `CreateProcess()` function call, which requires the path to be quoted to prevent unintended execution of files.

secure_coding_violation.rag: The vulnerable code block in `tools/sunshinesvc.cpp` initially constructs a command string without quoting the path to `sunshinesvc.exe`. This omission can lead to a security vulnerability where, if the path contains spaces, the `CreateProcess()` function might mistakenly execute a different executable, such as `C:\Program.exe`, if it exists. This is a violation of secure coding practices as it allows for potential path interception attacks. The patch addresses this by quoting the path, ensuring that `CreateProcess()` correctly interprets the intended executable path, thereby preventing unintended execution of malicious files.

mitigation.rag: Version 0.23.0 of Sunshine contains a patch for the issue. Workarounds include using application control tools like Windows Defender Application Control, AppLocker, or Software Restriction Policies to block potentially malicious software executed through path interception. Additionally, ensure proper permissions and directory access control are set to deny users the ability to write files to the top-level directory `C:`. It is required that all executables be placed in write-protected directories.

- **Functions or Files Involved**: The functions involved include `dwc3_gadget_giveback` and `ncm_unwrap_ntb`. The `ncm_unwrap_ntb` function is responsible for parsing the NTB and checking for leftover bytes in the SKB provided by `u_ether`.

- **Expected Behavior that Confirms Successful Exploitation**: Successful exploitation would result in the dropping of all datagrams that were properly parsed in the first NTB and saved in the `rx_list`, due to the presence of an unparsed extra byte.
